title: Redispatch rollout heuristics and minute watchboard
summary: Operational checklist and minute-by-minute watchboard for a redispatch-enabled rollout. Focus: graceful reroute, region-aware cadence, and telemetry thresholds for automated fallback.
body:
Purpose:
This working doc defines the heuristics and operational cadence for rollouts that may require live redispatching of traffic (route-level reroute to alternate model families / regions). It pairs a preflight checklist with a minute-by-minute watchboard and a short release-notes draft intended for customer-facing comms after stabilization.

Context / When to use:
- New model variant deployments that change memory/latency profiles (quantized variants, low-latency kernels).
- Cross-region model pinning changes where we may shift traffic between regions to avoid hotspots.
- Rolling out routing policy changes (latency-first -> cost-first) that touch traffic steering.

Preflight checklist (must be green before T0):
- [ ] Canary deploy for 1% traffic in us-west-2 (canary ID: canary-redispatch-2026-03)
- [ ] Load test replay 30m with historical QPS samples from last 7 days (run id: replay-2026-03-18)
- [ ] KV cache warmup script executed for top-10 prompt prefixes in production corpus (run: kv-warm-03-17)
- [ ] Cost-estimate delta confirmed with finance (sheet: deploy-cost-est-2026-Q2)
- [ ] Ops pager rotation confirmed and backup on-call assigned (primary: Marisol Vega, backup: Omar El-Amin)
- [ ] Slack channel + SMS bridge created: #deploy-redispatch-03-19 + bridge number in calendar invite
- [ ] Canary alerting thresholds set and verified in Prometheus/Alertmanager: latency p95 > 750ms, error rate > 0.7% over 2m -> page
- [ ] Telemetry sampling hooks set for trace IDs and model hash included in request logs
- [ ] Rollback runbook linked and smoke test scripts validated (runbook id: RB-2026-03-redispatch)

Rollout phases and cadence (high-level):
- T-30m: Final smoke run on staging, post-mortem anchor doc created
- T-5m: Announce in channel; confirm crew are paired and terminal-ready
- T0: Flip percent to 5% (canary) using gradual-traffic API (operator: Aisha)
- T+15m: If canary healthy -> 25% in us-west-2 and 5% in eu-west-1 (redispatch policy active)
- T+45m: If stable -> 50% and extend KV warmup for remaining prefixes
- T+90m: If stable -> 90% then full release at T+120m. If any step fails threshold -> immediate rollback to previous routing policy + trigger rollback smoke tests.

Minute-by-minute watchboard (operator view):
- 00:00 (T0) - Launch canary @5%: verify 200/200 ok for canary endpoint; check p50/p95/p99 for latency; verify sampling logs contain model-hash
- 02:00 - Canary traffic perf snapshot (2m window): check error rate, tail latency, and token generation stalls (>=1s between tokens)
- 05:00 - Canary metrics deeper dive: fetch traces for representative requests (search trace where prompt-length > 512 tokens)
- 10:00 - Telemetry: confirm KV cache hit-rate >= 65% for canary; if < 40% investigate cache warming path
- 15:00 - Decision point: escalate to 25% if all green; else hold and run extended diagnostic (call SRE)
- 30:00 - Redispatch sanity: confirm routing policy logs show expected fallback counts < 1%
- 45:00 - Resource checks: GPU utilization per-host < 85% and queue depth < 50 requests
- 60:00 - Extended canary snapshot & customer proxy testing (run synthetic against representative customers)
- 90:00 - Pre-fill capacity for final ramp; confirm autoscaler thresholds and burst tokens available
- 120:00 - Finalize release or execute rollback. If rollback, follow RB-2026-03-redispatch checklist and coordinate postmortem scheduling.

Automated thresholds and explicit escalation triggers:
- Immediate rollback triggers (automated):
  - error_rate_global > 0.75% sustained over 2m
  - p99 latency increases by > 2x vs baseline for 5m
  - model misclassification / hallucination metric increase > 12% on synthetic eval prompts (continuous eval)
- Manual escalation triggers (operator to page SRE):
  - repeated token stalls for multiple requests (>3 distinct traces in 10m)
  - sudden region capacity drop (instance preemptions or eviction)

Redispatch-specific heuristics (how we pick fallback):
- Prefer same-region compatible model variant for latency-sensitive customers (if variant exists + capacity)
- If local region capacity < 25% available, route to neighboring region with p50 additional latency < 150ms
- If cost-tier mismatch (dedicated -> hosted fallback), ensure request-level data classification flags allow cross-tenant processing
- Maintain sticky session for clients with > 10 requests/minute for the duration of the rollout to avoid double-switching

Telemetry dashboard widgets to monitor (links / names):
- "canary-latency-pctl" (p50/p95/p99 by region and route)
- "redispatch-fallback-counts" (per-model, per-region)
- "kv-cache-hitrate" (moving 5m window)
- "generation-stalls" (token-gap histogram)
- "errors-by-root-cause" (model, infra, network)

Runbook snippets (quick ops commands):
- View canary logs (last 30m): kubectl logs -l release=canary-redispatch --since=30m -n inference
- Force rollback traffic switch: curl -X POST $DEPLOY_API/traffic/switch -d '{"policy":"previous-stable"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Snapshot telemetry: ./scripts/snapshot-metrics.sh --selector canary-redispatch --window 5m --out /tmp/snap.json

Customer-facing release notes (draft):
Title: Rolling out smarter routing and new low-latency model variant (gradual, region-aware)
Summary: Today we begin a staged rollout of a new routing policy and a low-latency model variant designed to reduce high-traffic tail latency for real-time features. The rollout will be gradual and region-aware; we may temporarily route traffic to alternate regions for short intervals while we validate stability.
What changed:
- Added a new model variant: rdm-llv-8bit (optimized kernels for reduced generation tail latency)
- Introduced redispatch policy: routing can now fallback to region-compatible variants when local capacity drops below thresholds
Impact & expectations:
- Expected median latency reduction for interactive workloads: ~12–18% in peak windows
- No action required from customers; feature is opt-out via per-customer routing pin (contact support)
Known limitations (short):
- In some regions early customers may observe transient variance in p99 while KV caches rewarm (expected during first 2h)
- Customers with strict data residency (air-gapped / on-prem) will not be auto-redispatched without prior consent

Post-release followups (to schedule):
- 24h: Release digest + runbook snapshot attached to post-release ticket (owner: Aisha)
- 72h: Stability retro and metric bakeoff (participants: Eng, SRE, Product)
- 7d: Cost delta report and recommendation for whether to keep redispatch policy default for this model family

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Add a small synthetic suite that targets long-sequence prompts to better surface generation stalls during canaries
- Validate cross-tenant billing attribution when cross-region redispatch happens (finance check)
- Consider adding automatic sticky-window of 10m to avoid thrash when policy flips rapidly

Appendix: quick checklist for postmortem (if rollback):
- Collect full trace dump for the 30m leading to rollback
- Save autoscaler and cluster events for 2h window around rollout
- Export canary snapshot and attach to postmortem ticket (ENG-4821)

Notes: This doc is intentionally operational and intentionally terse — keep edits here lightweight. If we land on a stable pattern we should move a cleaned-up version into confluence: /display/infra/redispatch-playbook
